mainTopic: The חומש for a consecrated בהמה טמאה, and the משנה's list of laws measured by a פרוטה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a consecrated בהמה טמאה (non-kosher animal) and the extra חומש added when redeeming it. רבינא holds that the חומש applies only at the first stage of הקדש, not the middle stage. רב אחא מדיפתי and רב זוטרא challenge him. Logic could compare the middle stage to either the first or the last stage, so the גמרא settles it from the word ״הטמאה״, which means the first stage, just as רבא read ״העולה״. A ברייתא then supports רבי יהושע בן לוי and states that חומש is added only on the first הקדש. Next comes a new משנה giving the amounts for אונאה, a claim, an admission, and a list of five laws measured by a פרוטה. The גמרא explains why the משנה repeats earlier rules. It brings the argument between רב כהנא and לוי about whether אונאה applies to פרוטות, and compares our משנה's list with לוי's list to explain what each one leaves out. Finally the גמרא returns to רב קטינא, who says a בית דין hears even claims under a פרוטה. רבא begins an objection from a פסוק, and that objection continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Is the non-kosher animal not counted at the intermediate stage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a בהמה טמאה is not treated as part of אמצע הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not found at the intermediate stage of consecration?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing from the previous lines and asks a question to רבינא. Why is the בהמה טמאה not considered part of אמצע הקדש?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the rule of adding a חומש for a בהמה טמאה was tied to תחילת הקדש. Here someone asks why it should not also show up at the middle stage. This question sets up רבינא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated property; something dedicated to the בית המקדש
The intermediate (middle) stage of consecration
It is not there / it does not apply

phrases.english: At the intermediate stage of consecration, it is not found?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the non-kosher animal from the discussion just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section about a בהמה טמאה and the stages of הקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a בהמה טמאה is not considered to be at the intermediate stage of הקדש.

steps.title: Because it never reaches the final stage
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers: the בהמה טמאה has no final stage of הקדש, so it is not treated as having a middle stage either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because it is not found at the final stage of consecration.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question. Since a בהמה טמאה does not reach סוף הקדש, it does not count as being in the middle stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal cannot be brought as a קרבן, so it never stays holy in a final way. רבינא reasons that a 'middle' only makes sense if there is an 'end.' With no end, there is no real middle.

keyTerms.meaning: The final stage of consecration
Because

phrases.english: He said to him:
Because it is not found at the final stage of consecration.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּסוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A בהמה טמאה has no סוף הקדש, so it is not treated as part of אמצע הקדש.

steps.title: רב אחא: It is at the middle stage, so add the fifth
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי argues that the animal really does exist at the middle stage, so a חומש should be added there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: At least at the intermediate stage it exists, so let one also add a fifth!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges רבינא. Even if there is no final stage, the animal does exist at the middle stage, so why not add a חומש there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא does not accept that a missing end cancels the middle. In real life the animal does go through the middle stage. So the rule of חומש should apply there as well.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא from the town of Difti, an אמורא
At least / in any case
The extra fifth added when redeeming הקדש
So let him add

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא: מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא,
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
At the intermediate stage, at least, it exists,
so let one add a fifth as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the בהמה טמאה is not treated as being at אמצע הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal really does go through a middle stage. So the חומש rule should apply there too.

steps.title: The middle stage is treated like the final stage
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the middle stage is compared to the final stage. Just as there is no חומש at the end, there is none in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is like the final stage. Just as at the final stage one does not add a fifth, so too at the intermediate stage one does not add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends himself with a comparison. The middle stage follows the rules of סוף הקדש, and there is no חומש at סוף הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא now admits the animal may exist at the middle stage. But he says that stage follows the law of the final stage, not the first stage. So the חומש does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like / it has the same law as
Just as... so too... (a comparison form)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי הוּא כְּסוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: He said to him: It is like the final stage of consecration:

phrases.aramaic: מָה סוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ אֵינוֹ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ –
phrases.english: just as at the final stage one does not add a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֶמְצַע הֶקְדֵּשׁ אֵינוֹ מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: so too at the intermediate stage one does not add a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי הוּא כְּסוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison (היקש-style likening of one stage to another)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the animal is present at the middle stage, a חומש should be added there.
steps.terutzMaskana: The middle stage follows the law of the final stage, where there is no חומש.

steps.title: רב זוטרא: Why compare it to the end and not the beginning?
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בריה דרב מרי asks why רבינא chose to compare the middle stage to the final stage instead of the first stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בריה דרב מרי said to רבינא: What did you see that made you compare it to the final stage? Let us compare it to the initial stage!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge comes from רב זוטרא בריה דרב מרי. He asks why the middle stage should be like the end. Why not like the beginning, where a חומש is added?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's whole answer rested on a comparison. רב זוטרא points out that a middle stage sits between two others and could be compared to either one. If it were compared to תחילת הקדש, a חומש would be added.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why did you choose this option?)
That you compare
The initial stage of consecration
רב זוטרא son of רב מרי, an אמורא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Zutra son of Rav Mari said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי חָזֵית דִּמְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ לְסוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ?
phrases.english: What did you see that you compare it to the final stage of consecration?
Let us compare it to the initial stage of consecration!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חָזֵית דִּמְדַמֵּית לֵיהּ לְסוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison רבינא used in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's choice to compare אמצע הקדש to סוף הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The middle stage could just as well be compared to תחילת הקדש, where a חומש is added.

steps.title: Both got their holiness by transfer
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the middle stage is more like the final stage, because in both the holiness was transferred from something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It makes sense to compare it to the final stage, because we learn a 'caught' holiness from a 'caught' holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends his comparison. At both the middle and final stages, the holiness came by being 'caught' (transferred) from another item, so they are alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the first stage, the item is made holy directly. At the middle and final stages, the holiness passes onto the item from something else. Since they share this feature, רבינא says it is logical to compare the middle to the end.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason / it makes sense
Caught / took on holiness by transfer from another item
He should compare it

phrases.english: He said to him: It makes sense
that one should compare it to the final stage of consecration,
since we learn something 'caught' from something 'caught.'
phrases.notes: 'Caught' means the holiness was not placed on it directly. It moved onto it from a different holy item.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִסְתַּבְּרָא לְסוֹף הֶקְדֵּשׁ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְדַמּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב זוטרא's challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The middle stage could be compared to the first stage.
steps.terutzMaskana: The middle and final stages both have transferred (נתפס) holiness, so they are alike.

steps.title: On the contrary: both have another stage after them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite. The middle stage is like the first stage, because each has another stage of holiness that comes after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! One should compare it to the initial stage, because we learn something that has holiness after it from something that has holiness after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with its own reason. The first and middle stages both have more holiness coming after them, so maybe they belong together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two equal-strength reasons. The middle is like the end because both are 'caught' holiness. The middle is also like the beginning because both are followed by another stage. Logic alone cannot decide, which sets up the need for a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Something that has another stage of holiness after it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא has rejected רבינא's view here. It only shows that his logical comparison is not stronger than the opposite one. The next step settles the matter from the פסוק, and the result still matches רבינא's ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּה: לִתְחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְדַמּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: On the contrary: one should compare it to the initial stage of consecration,
since we learn something that has holiness after it
from something that has holiness after it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה: לִתְחִילַּת הֶקְדֵּשׁ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְדַמּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the סברא of step 6 with an opposite סברא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's reasoning that 'caught from caught' makes the middle stage like the final stage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An equally strong similarity links the middle stage to the first stage: both are followed by another stage of holiness.

steps.title: The word 'the' points to the first stage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles the question from the פסוק. Just as רבא learned that ״העולה״ means the first עולה, ״הטמאה״ means the first stage of the non-kosher animal's holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: 'The burnt-offering' means the first burnt-offering. So too, 'the non-kosher' animal means the initial stage of the non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the wording of the תורה. The extra word 'the' in ״הטמאה״ limits the חומש to the first stage, just as רבא read 'the' in ״העולה״ as meaning the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two logical comparisons cancel each other out, the גמרא turns to the text of the פסוק. The word 'the' (ה' הידיעה) points to one specific item, the first one. So the חומש is added only at תחילת הקדש, which supports רבינא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The burnt-offering (with the word 'the')
The first burnt-offering
The non-kosher (animal), with the word 'the'
So too / the same here

steps.whatToRemember: A חומש is added when redeeming a consecrated בהמה טמאה only at תחילת הקדש. Logic could pair the middle stage with either the beginning or the end. The deciding proof is the פסוק's word ״הטמאה״, which means the first stage, just like רבא's reading of ״העולה״.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא. When two סברות are equally strong, the question is decided by a small detail in the wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: As Rava said: 'The burnt-offering' means the first burnt-offering.
So too, 'the non-kosher' animal means the first stage of the non-kosher animal.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:27. This is the פסוק about redeeming a non-kosher animal and adding a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock between the two סברות in steps 6 and 7 by reading the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual derivation from the definite article (ה' הידיעה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The middle stage could be compared to the first stage, so a חומש would apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״הטמאה״ refers only to the first stage, so there is no חומש at the middle stage.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חומש for a consecrated בהמה טמאה applies only at תחילת הקדש, learned from the word ״הטמאה״.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי: a swap for a הקדש item works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that saying 'this cow in place of the הקדש cow' redeems the הקדש, and the הקדש treasury keeps the advantage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי: If someone says, 'This cow is in place of the הקדש cow,' or 'This garment is in place of the הקדש garment,' the הקדש is redeemed, and the הקדש treasury has the upper hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling that a redemption of הקדש takes effect even when the two items are not equal in value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not check whether the two items are worth the same, yet the ברייתא still says 'the הקדש is redeemed.' That backs רבי יהושע בן לוי. The words 'the הקדש has the upper hand' mean the treasury cannot lose. If the new item is worth less, the owner makes up the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
In place of, as an exchange for
His הקדש is redeemed (it loses its holiness)
The הקדש treasury has the upper hand and never loses out

steps.confusionAlert: 'הקדשו פדוי' does not mean the treasury takes a loss. The redemption works, but the treasury still gets full value.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with רבי יהושע בן לוי:
'This cow is in place of the cow of הקדש,'
or 'This garment is in place of the garment of הקדש' –
his הקדש is redeemed,
and the hand of הקדש is on top.
phrases.notes: He means the treasury always comes out ahead. If the new item is worth less, the owner pays the difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהושע בן לוי's earlier ruling about redeeming הקדש and brings a ברייתא that backs it.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling that a redemption of הקדש works even if the items are not equal in value
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about swapping a cow or garment in place of a הקדש one

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: a stated value, and חומש only on the first stage
steps.stepSummary: Even when the person names a price for the new item, the הקדש is redeemed. חומש is added on the first stage of holiness, not the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'This cow, worth five סלעים, is in place of the הקדש cow,' or 'This garment, worth five סלעים, is in place of the הקדש garment,' his הקדש is redeemed. On the first הקדש he adds חומש. On the second הקדש he does not add חומש.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to a case where the person names a price, and says the redemption still works. It then states plainly that חומש applies only to the first stage of holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a price that turns out wrong does not cancel the redemption. The second half says the same thing the גמרא worked out in steps 4 through 8. The original הקדש needs an extra חומש when redeemed. The item that took over its holiness does not.

keyTerms.meaning: סלעים, a type of silver coin
The first, original item that was made holy
The second item, which took on holiness when the first was redeemed onto it
Adds an extra fifth (חומש) when redeeming

steps.whatToRemember: Redeeming הקדש works even without an exact match in value, and the treasury never loses. חומש is added only for the first stage of holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא gives clear backing to the earlier conclusion that there is no חומש on a second stage of holiness.

phrases.english: 'This cow, valued at five סלעים,'
is in place of the cow of הקדש,'
or 'This garment, valued at five סלעים,
is in place of the garment of הקדש' –
his הקדש is redeemed.
On the first הקדש he adds a fifth,

phrases.aramaic: עַל הֶקְדֵּשׁ שֵׁנִי אֵין מוֹסִיף חוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: on the second הקדש he does not add a fifth.
phrases.notes: The 'second' is the new cow or garment that took over the holiness. Redeeming it later needs no extra fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרָה זוֹ בְּחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים תַּחַת פָּרָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding the stated-price case and the חומש rule.
steps.raayaObject: The redemption works even with a stated price, and there is no חומש on a second stage of holiness
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ברייתא

steps.title: New משנה: the amounts for אונאה, a claim, and an admission
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets אונאה at four silver מעה, the smallest claim for an oath at two silver מעה, and the smallest admission at a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: אונאה is four silver מעה. A claim is two silver מעה. An admission is a שוה פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives three key amounts of money used in Jewish law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אונאה is four מעה out of the 24 מעה in a סלע, which is one sixth. For a court oath, the claim must be at least two silver מעה. The defendant's admission to part of it must be at least a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה
Overcharging or underpaying in a sale
A claim brought against someone in court
An admission (owning up to part of the claim)
The value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin

steps.confusionAlert: 'Four כסף' and 'two כסף' mean silver מעה, small coins, not full silver shekels.

phrases.english: משנה: Overcharging – four silver [מעה],
phrases.notes: That is four out of the 24 מעה in a סלע, one sixth.

phrases.english: and the claim – two silver [מעה],
and the admission – the value of a פרוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הקדש discussion and opens a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אונאה is four silver מעה, a claim is two silver מעה, and an admission is a שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: The משנה lists five laws that use a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: Five laws have a שוה פרוטה as their minimum: admission, קידושין, מעילה, announcing a found object, and returning a stolen item after a false oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are five פרוטות: An admission is a שוה פרוטה. A woman can be betrothed with a שוה פרוטה. Someone who benefits from הקדש by a שוה פרוטה has done מעילה. Someone who finds something worth a פרוטה must announce it. Someone who stole a שוה פרוטה from his friend and swore falsely to him must bring it to him even as far as מדי.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the משנה just mentioned a פרוטה for an admission, it now lists all five laws where a פרוטה is the amount that counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has the same minimum, a שוה פרוטה, but the laws themselves are different. The last case is the strictest. A thief who also swore falsely must return the item to the owner himself, even if he must travel to faraway מדי.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes betrothed (קידושין)
Has done מעילה, wrongfully used holy property
To announce a found object
One who steals by force or in the open
To מדי, a faraway land

steps.whatToRemember: A שוה פרוטה is the smallest amount the law counts. It is the minimum for admission, קידושין, מעילה, announcing a lost object, and returning stolen property after a false oath.
steps.whyThisMatters: The case of the thief who swore falsely shows how far a person must go to fix a theft that was covered up with an oath.

phrases.english: There are five פרוטות:
the admission is a שוה פרוטה,
and a woman is betrothed with a שוה פרוטה,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַנֶּהֱנֶה בְּשָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ מָעַל,
phrases.english: and one who benefits a שוה פרוטה from הקדש has done מעילה,
and one who finds a שוה פרוטה must announce it,
and one who robs his fellow of a שוה פרוטה
and swore to him [falsely that he did not],
must carry it after him even to מדי.
phrases.notes: He has to hand it back to the owner himself, wherever the owner is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the פרוטה mentioned for an admission and lists all five laws that use that amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five laws use a שוה פרוטה as their minimum: admission, קידושין, מעילה, announcing a found object, and returning stolen property after a false oath (even to מדי).

steps.title: Why repeat the measure of overcharging?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why our משנה repeats the rule of four silver מעה, since an earlier משנה already taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We already learned this once: overcharging is four silver מעה out of the twenty-four in a סלע, which is one-sixth of the sale!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה: why teach the four-מעה rule again when we already learned it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה already said that אונאה is one-sixth, which for a סלע is four out of twenty-four מעה. A משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason, so the repetition needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned it (in a משנה)
One time, already once
One-sixth
A coin worth twenty-four silver מעה

phrases.english: GEMARA: We already learned this one time:
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier משנה on 49b about how much overcharging counts.

phrases.english: Overcharging is four silver [מעה]
out of the twenty-four silver [מעה] in a סלע,
one-sixth of the sale!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first rule of the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The four-מעה rule of אונאה in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It was already taught in an earlier משנה, so repeating it seems pointless.

steps.title: The repetition was needed for the oath rules
steps.stepSummary: The משנה repeats אונאה only to bring along the new rules about the claim and admission for an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule of the claim of two silver מעה and the admission of a פרוטה's worth was what the תנא needed to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the main point of the משנה was the oath rules, and אונאה was mentioned just alongside them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new information is the smallest claim (two silver מעה) and the smallest admission (a פרוטה) that obligate an oath. The אונאה rule was repeated only as part of a list of money amounts.

keyTerms.meaning: The claim the plaintiff makes in court
The defendant's admission to part of the claim
He needed it, it was necessary to teach

phrases.english: The claim of two silver [מעה]
and the admission of a פרוטה's worth
is what he needed [to teach].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repeated rule comes along with a new rule that needed teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה repeated the אונאה rule for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real purpose was the oath amounts, and אונאה was listed with them.

steps.title: The oath rules were also taught already
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the oath amounts are also taught in another משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That too we already learned: the judges' oath is when the claim is two silver מעה and the admission is a פרוטה's worth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the oath rules are not new either, since a משנה in שבועות already teaches them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the oath amounts were the new point. But they appear in משנה שבועות, so the question returns: why repeat anything here?

keyTerms.meaning: The oath the judges impose on a defendant who admits part of a claim
This too

phrases.english: That too we already learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שבועות 38b.

phrases.english: The judges' oath:
the claim is two silver [מעה]
and the admission is a פרוטה's worth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the oath amounts were the new point
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those amounts are already in משנה שבועות, so they are also a repetition.

steps.title: The new point is the list of five פרוטות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה needed its last part, the list of five פרוטות, which is not taught anywhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא needed the end of the משנה, which teaches: there are five פרוטות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the truly new part is the end of the משנה, the list of five laws that use a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rules were repeated only to lead into the end of the משנה. The list of five פרוטות, taught in step 12, is found only here.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
Which teaches

steps.whatToRemember: Each repetition in our משנה is explained by the new rule it leads to, ending with the list of five פרוטות.

phrases.english: He needed the end of the משנה,
which teaches: There are five פרוטות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repeated rules lead into a new rule at the end of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even the oath amounts are a pointless repetition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה builds up to the list of five פרוטות, which is new.

steps.title: Why is overcharging not on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the list of five פרוטות does not include אונאה of a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "There are five פרוטות," etc. Then let it also teach that overcharging is a פרוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the list of five פרוטות and asks why אונאה of a פרוטה is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list gives the laws where a פרוטה is the smallest amount that matters. The גמרא wonders why אונאה is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it also teach
The smallest coin that counts as money

phrases.english: "There are five פרוטות," etc.
Then let it also teach: overcharging is a פרוטה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the list of five פרוטות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the list collects laws measured by a פרוטה, אונאה of a פרוטה seems to be missing.

steps.title: רב כהנא: no overcharging for פרוטות
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא learns from the missing case that אונאה does not apply to amounts of just פרוטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: This tells us that there is no overcharging for פרוטות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא explains that אונאה is left off the list on purpose, because it does not apply to small amounts of פרוטות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's silence becomes a source for a rule. A price gap of only a few פרוטות does not count as אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא
This tells us, we learn from here
There is no overcharging for amounts of פרוטות

phrases.english: רב כהנא said:
This tells us,
there is no overcharging for פרוטות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The missing case teaches a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have listed אונאה of a פרוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was left out because there is no אונאה for פרוטות.

steps.title: לוי: there is overcharging for פרוטות
steps.stepSummary: לוי disagrees with רב כהנא and holds that אונאה does apply to פרוטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי said: There is overcharging for פרוטות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings לוי, who disagrees with רב כהנא and says אונאה applies even to amounts of פרוטות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a direct argument with step 18. For לוי, even a small gap of פרוטות can count as אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time between the תנאים and the אמוראים
There is overcharging for amounts of פרוטות

phrases.english: And לוי said:
There is overcharging for פרוטות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion to רב כהנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אונאה applies even to amounts of פרוטות.

steps.title: לוי's version of the משנה lists overcharging
steps.stepSummary: In לוי's own collection of משניות, the list of five פרוטות includes אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so לוי taught in his collection of משניות: There are five פרוטות: overcharging is a פרוטה, admission is a פרוטה, betrothing a woman is with a פרוטה, robbery is with a פרוטה, and the judges sit for a case of a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that לוי's view matches his own version of the משנה, where אונאה is on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, אונאה is missing, which supports רב כהנא. In לוי's version, אונאה is listed, which fits his view that אונאה applies to פרוטות.

keyTerms.meaning: And so he taught
His collection of משניות
Betrothing a woman
The judges sitting to hear a case

steps.confusionAlert: לוי's list is not the same as our משנה's list. It adds אונאה and judges sitting, and does not list מעילה or announcing a found object.
steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא says there is no אונאה for פרוטות, based on our משנה. לוי says there is, and his version of the משנה lists it.

phrases.english: And so לוי taught in his collection of משניות:
There are five פרוטות:
overcharging is a פרוטה, admission is a פרוטה,
betrothing a woman is with a פרוטה,
robbery is with a פרוטה,
phrases.notes: This means someone who falsely swears he didn't steal. The rule applies if he stole at least a פרוטה.

phrases.english: and the judges sit for a case of a פרוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports לוי's opinion from step 19.
steps.raayaObject: לוי's view that there is אונאה for פרוטות
steps.raayaSupportSource: לוי's own version of the משנה, which lists אונאה among the five פרוטות
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument between רב כהנא and לוי goes back to two different versions of the same list.

steps.title: Why does our משנה leave out the court case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא of our משנה does not list ישיבת הדיינין among the five פרוטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא: why doesn't he teach the case of judges sitting to hear a claim?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to our own משנה. It asks why our list leaves out ישיבת הדיינין, the rule that a court hears a claim worth a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי's list (Step 20) shows there were other פרוטה cases a תנא could have listed. Now the גמרא wants to know why our תנא chose not to list the court case.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא: the author of our משנה
The sitting of the judges: a court agreeing to hear a case
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And our תנא,
what is the reason he does not teach
the sitting of the judges?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא דִּידַן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After seeing לוי's fuller list, the גמרא asks why our משנה leaves out a case that לוי includes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of five פרוטות in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A court hearing a claim worth a פרוטה is a real 'פרוטה rule', so why isn't it on the list?

steps.title: Robbery already covers it
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא taught גזל, and that already covers every money claim, including the court case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the court case is already included in the case of גזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any money claim someone brings to court is like a claim that the other person is holding his money. Since the משנה already said a פרוטה counts for גזל, there was no need to list the court case separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbery: taking or holding someone else's money
He has already taught it

phrases.english: He taught robbery.
phrases.notes: Robbery covers any money claim against another person, so the court case is already included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The missing case is already included in another listed case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court case was simply forgotten from our list.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is covered by גזל, so listing it would repeat something already taught.

steps.title: But then why list lost property?
steps.stepSummary: If גזל covers all money cases, why does our משנה also list אבידה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't he teach robbery and still also teach lost property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Our משנה lists both גזל and אבידה, so it seems the תנא does list cases even when גזל already covers them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'גזל covers it' were enough of a reason, אבידה should have been left out too. The fact that אבידה is listed weakens the answer in Step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost object
But doesn't he...? (a phrase that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But doesn't he teach robbery
and still teach lost property?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי לָא תָּנֵי גָּזֵל וְקָתָנֵי אֲבֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that גזל covers all money cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה itself lists אבידה next to גזל, so it does not leave out cases just because גזל covers them.

steps.title: Robbery and lost property each teach something new
steps.stepSummary: גזל and אבידה each have a special new point, so both had to be listed. The court case has no such new point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those two were needed. Robbery: one who robs his friend of a פרוטה's worth and swears falsely to him must bring it to him, even as far as מדי. Lost property: one who finds a lost object worth a פרוטה must announce it, even if it later went down in value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that גזל and אבידה were each listed because each one teaches its own new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For גזל, the new rule is that a robber who swore falsely must return even a פרוטה, even if he has to travel far to the owner. For אבידה, the new rule is that the finder must announce it even if its value later dropped below a פרוטה. The court case adds nothing like this, so גזל covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him (it teaches something new)
And swore to him (falsely denied it with an oath)
He must bring it after him (to wherever the owner is)
To announce a found object
That it went down in value

steps.whatToRemember: A תנא lists a case even when it seems covered by another case, if it has its own new point. גזל and אבידה each have one.

phrases.english: Those were necessary for him:
Robbery: one who robs his friend of a פרוטה's worth
and swore to him,
must bring it after him, even to Media.
phrases.notes: מדי was a land very far away. He must return it even if that means a long trip.

phrases.english: Lost property: one who finds a lost object worth a פרוטה
is obligated to announce it,
even though it went down in value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 and so defends the answer of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each listed case teaches its own new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing אבידה shows the תנא repeats cases that גזל already covers.
steps.terutzMaskana: אבידה and גזל each add a new rule. The court case adds nothing, so it was left out.

steps.title: Why does לוי leave out lost property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why לוי's list does not include אבידה worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי: why doesn't he teach lost property worth a פרוטה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question about לוי's list. Why is אבידה missing from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists אבידה but לוי does not. The גמרא wants to know why לוי left it out.

keyTerms.meaning: With a פרוטה (worth a פרוטה)

phrases.english: And לוי, what is the reason
he does not teach lost property worth a פרוטה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵוִי, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי אֲבֵידָה בִּפְרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same question asked of our משנה in Step 21 is now asked of לוי's list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אבידה has a real פרוטה rule, as our משנה shows, so why is it missing from לוי's list?

steps.title: Robbery covers lost property for לוי
steps.stepSummary: לוי taught גזל, and that already covers אבידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: לוי's case of גזל already covers אבידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Keeping a lost object without returning it is like holding someone else's money. So in לוי's view, listing גזל was enough.

phrases.english: He taught robbery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25, the same way Step 22 answered Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The missing case is already included in another listed case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי did not agree with the פרוטה rule for אבידה.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי left out אבידה only because גזל already covers it.

steps.title: But then why does לוי list the court case?
steps.stepSummary: If גזל covers all money cases, why does לוי list ישיבת הדיינין too?
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't he teach robbery and still also teach the sitting of the judges?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. לוי lists both גזל and ישיבת הדיינין, even though Step 22 said גזל covers the court case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of Step 23. If גזל covers everything, the court case should not need its own place on לוי's list.

phrases.english: But doesn't he teach robbery
and still teach the sitting of the judges?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי לָא קָתָנֵי גָּזֵל וְקָתָנֵי יְשִׁיבַת הַדַּיָּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that גזל covers all money cases in לוי's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוי lists the court case next to גזל, so he does not leave out cases just because גזל covers them.

steps.title: The court case is listed to reject רב קטינא
steps.stepSummary: לוי needed to list ישיבת הדיינין to reject רב קטינא, who says a בית דין hears cases even for less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sitting of the judges was necessary for him, to reject the view of רב קטינא. For רב קטינא said: a court takes up a case even for less than a פרוטה's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the court case does teach something new in לוי's list. It shows that a court needs at least a פרוטה, which goes against רב קטינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב קטינא holds that a בית דין will hear a claim even if it is worth less than a פרוטה. By listing 'judges sit for a פרוטה', לוי teaches that a פרוטה is the minimum. That is why the court case needed its own place on his list, while אבידה did not.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (to reject another view)
An אמורא quoted here
Take up, attend to (a case)
Less than a פרוטה's worth

steps.whatToRemember: Each list leaves out what גזל covers. Each one keeps a case only if it has its own new point. Our משנה keeps גזל and אבידה. לוי keeps the court case to reject רב קטינא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two lists are not random. Each list's choices match what that list comes to teach.

phrases.english: The sitting of the judges was necessary for him,
to reject the view of רב קטינא,
phrases.notes: לוי's list teaches that a court needs at least a פרוטה, which goes against רב קטינא.

phrases.english: for רב קטינא said:
a court takes up a case
even for less than a פרוטה's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְשִׁיבַת הַדַּיָּינִין אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 27 and so defends the answer of Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The listed case teaches a new point by rejecting another opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing the court case shows that לוי repeats cases that גזל already covers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court case adds a new rule: a court needs at least a פרוטה, which rejects רב קטינא.

steps.title: Why does לוי leave out consecrated property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why לוי's list does not include the פרוטה rule of הקדש, which our משנה does list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי, why doesn't he teach the case of consecrated property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps comparing the two lists. It asks why לוי's list is missing the הקדש case that our משנה includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists הקדש as one of the cases where a פרוטה matters. If לוי is also listing פרוטה cases, the הקדש case seems to be missing from his list.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not teach (it is not in his list)

phrases.english: And לוי, what is the reason
that he does not teach consecrated property?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining what לוי does list, the גמרא now asks about something he leaves out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה counts הקדש as a פרוטה case, so לוי's list looks incomplete without it.

steps.title: לוי only deals with ordinary property
steps.stepSummary: לוי's list deals only with non-holy property, so הקדש does not belong in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is talking about non-holy property; he is not talking about holy property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that לוי's whole list is about ordinary property. Holy property is simply outside his topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is missing from לוי's list. He chose to deal only with חולין, so the הקדש case is not part of what he set out to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy property
Holy, consecrated things
He is talking about

phrases.english: He is speaking about non-holy property;
he is not speaking about holy property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי's list should cover every פרוטה case, including הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי's list covers only חולין, so הקדש is outside it.

steps.title: Why doesn't our משנה list מעשר שני?
steps.stepSummary: Since our משנה does deal with holy things, it should also list that מעשר שני is redeemed with a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But our תנא, who does talk about holy things, should teach that מעשר is redeemed for a פרוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the question turns to our משנה. If it deals with holy things like הקדש, why doesn't it also list the פרוטה rule of מעשר שני?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about לוי means that a list dealing with holy things should include all the holy cases. Our משנה includes הקדש, so leaving out מעשר שני now looks like a gap.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of our משנה
Here: מעשר שני, the tithe that can be redeemed with money
Let him teach (it should be in the list)

phrases.english: But our תנא,
who does speak about holy things,
let him teach: tithe for a פרוטה!
phrases.notes: He means that מעשר שני can be redeemed only if it is worth at least a פרוטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תַּנָּא דִּידַן דְּקָא מַיְירֵי בְּקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 30 and turns it against our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's list of פרוטה cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If our משנה deals with קדשים, it should list every holy case that needs a פרוטה, including מעשר שני.

steps.title: Our משנה holds מעשר needs more than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה follows the view that מעשר שני is redeemed only when its added fifth is worth a פרוטה, so the minimum is more than one פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows the one who says: if its fifth is not worth a פרוטה, it is not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows a view in which מעשר שני needs more than one פרוטה. So it does not fit a list of things that need just one פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this view, the added fifth must itself be worth a פרוטה. That means the מעשר must be worth several פרוטות. Since one פרוטה is not the minimum, מעשר שני does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Its fifth (the extra fifth added when redeeming your own מעשר)

phrases.english: In line with the one who says:
if its fifth is not worth a פרוטה [it is not redeemed].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets aren't actually said; the גמרא expects you to fill them in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the source within a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעשר שני is redeemed with a פרוטה, so it belongs in the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: By our משנה's view, מעשר שני needs more than a פרוטה, so it is not a 'one פרוטה' case.

steps.title: Then list 'the fifth of מעשר is a פרוטה'
steps.stepSummary: If the rule is that the fifth must be a פרוטה, the משנה could list that as a פרוטה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it teach: the fifth of מעשר must be worth a פרוטה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Even by this view there is still a פרוטה rule here, about the fifth, so why not list that?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer explained why the full value of מעשר is not on the list. But the fifth itself does have a one-פרוטה minimum, so it seems it could still be listed.

keyTerms.meaning: A fifth, the extra amount added when redeeming
And let him teach

phrases.english: Then let him teach: the fifth of tithe is a פרוטה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that מעשר follows the 'its fifth is a פרוטה' view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That view still has a one-פרוטה rule (for the fifth), so the משנה could have listed it.

steps.title: The משנה deals with the main amount, not the fifth
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה lists only rules about the main amount (קרן), not about the added fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is talking about the principal; he is not talking about the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה's list only deals with the main value of things. The extra fifth is outside its topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the cases in the משנה are about the main amount needing a פרוטה. A rule about the added fifth is a different kind of rule, so it was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal, the main amount

steps.whatToRemember: Each list is limited to its own topic: לוי deals only with חולין, and our משנה deals only with the main amount (קרן). That is why some פרוטה rules are left out of each list.

phrases.english: He is speaking about the principal;
he is not speaking about the fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקַרְנָא קָא מַיְירֵי, בְּחוֹמֶשׁ לָא קָא מַיְירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33 and closes the comparison of the lists.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule about the fifth of מעשר should be on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only rules about the קרן, so the fifth is left out.

steps.title: רב קטינא: a בית דין hears even cases under a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב קטינא's ruling, mentioned earlier, that a בית דין takes up cases worth even less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself. רב קטינא said: a בית דין takes up cases even for less than the value of a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to look closely at רב קטינא's ruling, which was mentioned in step 28. This is setting up a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב קטינא was mentioned only to explain why לוי listed ישיבת הדיינין. Now the גמרא examines his ruling on its own terms: the court will hear a claim even if it is worth less than a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the matter itself (a statement quoted earlier in passing)
The אמורא who says a court hears cases under a פרוטה
Take up, attend to (a case)
Less than the value of a פרוטה

phrases.english: The matter itself: רב קטינא said:
A court takes up a case
even for less than the value of a פרוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that examines the ruling quoted in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין hears monetary claims even for less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: רבא begins an objection from a פסוק about הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to challenge רב קטינא by quoting the פסוק about paying back what one took from holy property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection: 'And what he sinned with from the holy thing, he shall pay.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins an objection to רב קטינא by quoting a פסוק. This line only sets up the challenge; the rest of it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far רבא has only quoted the פסוק about paying back for misusing holy property. The point of his challenge against רב קטינא will be spelled out in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a source)
The אמורא raising the objection
He shall pay back

phrases.english: רבא raised an objection:
'And that which he sinned from the holy thing, he shall pay,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attack on the ruling stated in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב קטינא's ruling that a בית דין hears cases under a פרוטה
